comment: The summary of relationships says that a component is “composed of the functions and data objects it contains.” In ArchiMate, composition and access relationships have different meanings. A component accesses data objects rather than necessarily containing them.

public.text: The summary of relationships says that a component is “composed of the functions and data objects it contains.” In ArchiMate, composition and access relationships have different meanings. A component accesses data objects rather than necessarily containing them.
public.suggestedRevision: Correct the explanation so that composition is used for true whole-part relationships, while access represents reading, writing, or otherwise interacting with data objects. Ensure the diagrams and machine-readable model use the same distinction.
